issues.where: foreground shallows and the wet-sand edge during the six-second camera hold
issues.what: The foreground waterline and the large reflection shapes stay effectively pinned while animals cross the midground, so the shoreline reads like part of a still image.
issues.fix: Send irregular, low ripples through the shallows and let thin sheets of water advance and drain around the stones, bending the reflections as they pass.

issues.where: the two near-right flyers at frames 2401–2412, also visible in set-B-02.png
issues.what: The wings change angle considerably but the bodies barely pitch or rise in response, making the strokes look hinged onto hovering models.
issues.fix: Couple each stroke to a small body pitch and lift, with recovery and glide timed separately for each animal.

issues.where: cloud bank between the rear spires during the six-second hold
issues.what: The distant cloud silhouettes hold their shape and position while the near spray and flyers change, leaving the sky reading as a fixed backdrop.
issues.fix: Give the cloud layers slow, independent drift and subtle changes at their edges without moving the rock silhouettes.
